slides.texte_overlay:
Why a short nap can
change your whole afternoon
Keep it short. Fifteen to twenty minutes is enough. Longer naps send you into deep sleep and leave you groggy.
Time it right. Early afternoon, around the natural dip after lunch. Napping late in the day can ruin your night.
Set an alarm. Knowing you'll wake up helps you relax and fall asleep faster. Twenty minutes, then up, even if you feel like staying.
Make it dark and quiet. A sleep mask, earplugs or a quiet corner. Even a short rest in a calm place helps. Find your spot.
Before: afternoons felt slow and foggy. After: a short rest and five minutes a day of history, art or science, and my head feels clearer.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: afternoons felt slow and foggy. After: a short rest and I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. My head feels clearer.

slides.texte_overlay: Try a coffee nap. Drink a coffee, then nap for fifteen minutes. You wake up just as the caffeine starts working.
Don't use naps to replace sleep. A good night is still the base. Naps are a bonus, not a fix. Sleep well at night first.
